title: BM, 2025'te göç yollarında yaklaşık 8 bin kişinin öldüğünü veya kaybolduğunu bildirdi
summary: Uluslararası Göç Örgütü (IOM), 2025'te dünya genelindeki göç yollarında yaklaşık 8 bin kişinin hayatını kaybettiğini veya kaybolduğunu, bu yıl 15 Eylül itibarıyla ise en az 2 bin 292 kişinin öldüğünü veya kaybolduğunu açıkladı. IOM, düzensiz göç ve göç yollarındaki can kayıplarına ilişkin yazılı açıklama yaptı. Açıklamada, 2025'te dünya genelindeki göç yollarında yaklaşık 8 bin kişinin hayatını kaybettiği veya kaybolduğu belirtildi. Bu yıl 15 Eylül itibarıyla deniz yoluyla Avrupa'ya gelenlerin sayısının yüzde 39 azaldığı kaydedilen açıklamada, buna rağmen en az 2 bin 292 kişinin öldüğü veya kaybolduğu bildirildi. Geçen yılın aynı döneminde bu sayının 1.999 olduğu ifade edildi. Ülkelere işbirliği çağrısı IOM açıklamasında ülkelere, göç yollarında karşılaşılan ortak sorunların ve fırsatların ele alınması çağrısında bulunuldu. Hayat kurtarmak, insan ticareti ve kaçakçılıkla mücadele etmek ve güvenli göç yollarını genişletmek için ülkelerin birlikte hareket etmesinin gerekliliğine dikkat çekildi. Bu yıl 22-28 Eylül tarihlerinde 81'incisi düzenlenecek Birleşmiş Milletler (BM) Genel Kurulu'na katılacak ülkelere de göç konusunda ortak mücadele çağrısı yapıldı. Açıklamada, herkes için işe yarayan çözümler geliştirilmesinin hedeflendiği belirtildi. "Kaçakçılar ülkeler arasındaki boşluklardan yararlanıyor" IOM Genel Direktörü Amy Pope, insan kaçakçılarının sınırları dikkate almadığını ve sınırları kendi faaliyetleri için bir rota olarak gördüğünü belirtti. Pope, "Kaçakçılar, önceden plan yapar ve ülkeler arasındaki boşluklardan yararlanmak için harekete geçer. Ülkeler birlikte çalıştığında hayat kurtarabilir, suç şebekelerini bozabilir ve sınırlarını daha etkili şekilde yönetebilir. (BM Genel Kurulu'nda) Bu, bu hafta masaya yatırdığımız ana konulardan biri." ifadelerini kullandı. AA BM GÖÇ Birleşmiş Milletler Uluslararası Göç Örgütü (IOM), 2025'te göç yollarında yaklaşık 8 bin kişinin öldüğünü veya kaybolduğunu belirterek, ülkelere "insan ticareti ve kaçakçılıkla mücadele için birlikte çalışma" çağrısında bulundu Pazartesi, Eylül 21, 2026 - 19:15 Main image: Fotoğraf: AA Dünya Type: news SEO Title: BM, 2025'te göç yollarında yaklaşık 8 bin kişinin öldüğünü veya kaybolduğunu bildirdi copyright Independentturkish:

title: İstanbul Barosu “Ailem Güvende” operasyonları ile ilgili raporunu açıkladı
summary: İstanbul Barosu İnsan Hakları Merkezi, Kadın Hakları Merkezi ve Avukat Hakları Merkezi, 12 Eylül 2026’da “Ailem Güvende” gerekçesiyle başlatılan operasyonlarda yaşanan hak ihlallerine ilişkin rapor hazırladı. Operasyon kapsamında 7’si avukat 107 kişinin gözaltına alındığı belirtildi. Rapor, düzenlenen basın toplantısıyla kamuoyuna açıklandı. Açıklamayı İstanbul Barosu Kadın Hakları Merkezi’nden Diren Cevahir Şen okudu. Operasyonlara ilişkin tespitler Raporda, 12 Eylül’den itibaren kurumlar, aktivistler ve gazetecilere yönelik müdahalelerin; internet siteleri ve sosyal medya hesaplarına erişim engelleri, dernek, işletme ve konutlarda arama ve el koyma işlemleri ile ceza soruşturmaları, gözaltı ve tutuklamalar olmak üzere üç başlıkta gerçekleştiği belirtildi. 12 Eylül’ü 13 Eylül’e bağlayan gece dernek, ev ve mekanlara eş zamanlı operasyonlar yapıldığı, bazı dernek ofisleri ile kişilerin evlerinde arama gerçekleştirildiği ve dijital cihazlara el konulduğu aktarıldı. Soruşturmalarda “suç işlemek amacıyla örgüt kurma”, “uyuşturucu”, “müstehcenlik”, “fuhuş” ve “Dernekler Kanunu’na muhalefet” suçlamalarının yöneltildiği belirtildi. İstanbul’da 35 kişi gözaltına alındı Raporda, İstanbul’da altı sivil toplum kuruluşuna yönelik işlemler yürütüldüğü, sivil toplum örgütü yöneticileri ve üyelerinin gözaltına alındığı ifade edildi. İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı’nın soruşturmayı “çocukların üstün yararı”, “ailenin korunması” ve “toplumun ortak ahlaki değerleri” gerekçeleriyle ilişkilendirdiği aktarılan raporda, İstanbul’da 35 kişinin gözaltına alındığı ve 20 kişinin tutuklandığı belirtildi. Rapora göre operasyon kapsamında 6 dernek ve 10 işletme hakkında da işlem yapıldı. Ayrıca 11 LGBTİ+ derneğinin internet sitesinin yanı sıra 32 X hesabı ve 419 sosyal medya hesabının erişime engellendiği, 107 hesap için daha erişim engeli talep edildiği kaydedildi. Soruşturma dosyalarına erişim engeli Raporda, operasyonlar kapsamında başlatılan soruşturma dosyalarında gizlilik kararı alındığı ve avukatların dosyalara erişiminin engellendiği belirtildi. Dosya içeriğinin basınla paylaşılması nedeniyle kişilerin lekelenmeme hakkının ihlal edildiği savunulan raporda, dernekler ve hak savunucularının soyut ve belirsiz gerekçelerle kriminalize edilmeye çalışıldığı ifade edildi. Raporda ayrıca, 15 Eylül’de Çağlayan Adliyesi önünde operasyonları protesto etmek amacıyla basın açıklaması yapmak isteyen yurttaşların gözaltına alındığı belirtildi. 107 kişinin gözaltına alındığı, bunlardan 58’inin İstanbul Emniyet Müdürlüğü Asayiş Şube Müdürlüğüne, 40’ının Küçükçekmece Polis Merkezine sevk edildiği, 9 kişinin ise İstanbul İl Emniyet Müdürlüğü Güvenlik Şubesinde tutulduğu aktarıldı. Avukatların görevlerini yapmasının engellendiği belirtildi Raporda, gözaltına alınan 107 kişiden 7’sinin İstanbul Barosuna kayıtlı avukat olduğu belirtildi. 106 kişinin ifadelerinin tamamlanmasına rağmen gözaltı süresinin 24 saat uzatıldığı kaydedilen raporda, gözaltı sürecinde ters kelepçe, darp, kötü muamele, sağlık hizmetlerine erişim ve avukatlarla görüşme konusunda çeşitli hak ihlalleri yaşandığı yönündeki tespitlere yer verildi. Avukatların, gözaltındaki müvekkilleriyle görüşmek için İstanbul İl Emniyet Müdürlüğüne girişlerinin yaklaşık 9,5 saat engellendiği de raporda yer aldı. Gözaltındaki kişilere su ve yemek verilmediği, dışarıdan yemek tesliminin engellendiği ve vegan ile vejetaryen kişilerin beslenme taleplerinin karşılanmadığı yönündeki beyanlara da raporda yer verildi. “Ailelerin temel sorunları ekonomik sorunlardır” Basın toplantısında konuşan Avukat Hakları Merkezi Başkanı Mustafa Rüzgar da avukatların emniyet müdürlüklerine girişinin engellendiğini ve görevlerini yapmalarının zorlaştırıldığını söyledi. Rüzgar, gözaltına alınan yurttaşların tutulma süreçlerine ilişkin yapılan tespitlerde kötü muamele ve işkence izleri bulunduğunu ileri sürdü. Bu konularla ilgili yasal süreçlerin başlatılacağını belirtti. “Ailem Güvende” operasyonuna da değinen Rüzgar, ailelerin sorunlarının düşünce ve ifade özgürlüğüyle ilgili olmadığını savundu. Rüzgar, ailelerin temel sorunlarının güvenli konuta, beslenmeye, gıdaya erişim ve ekonomik sorunlar olduğunu belirterek, insanların düşüncelerine, yaşam biçimlerine ve varoluşlarına yönelik müdahaleleri kabul etmediklerini ifade etti. title: Die Mythen. Chapter 33: Merits
summary: ​Chapter 33: Merits ​"A warm welcome to our capital. We are immensely honored that Prosperity Bank chose Warsaw of all places as the site of its headquarters in this part of Europe," the city mayor solemnly proclaimed, turning toward the lenses of over a dozen cameras with a practiced smile. ​The flash of cameras reflected in the polished granite lobby of the skyscraper at Rondo Daszyńskiego. With a quiet, dry snap, the scissors sliced through the thick ribbon, clearing the path to the elevators leading to the top floors, where the management of the new financial powerhouse was housed. ​The man standing beside the city's leader looked impeccable. A suit of Italian wool fit him like a second skin, and an understated signet ring set with a black stone drew the eyes of female journalists. An unnatural, predatory elegance radiated from him. ​"Thank you, Mr. Mayor," he replied in a deep, velvety timbre. He accepted the microphone with cosmopolitan grace. "The Polish market is pivotal to our institution. I personally took the trouble to master your language. Please forgive my harsh, foreign accent; it is an exceedingly difficult tongue. I hope, however, that Prosperity Bank will become for Warsaw and its residents not only a symbol of stability, but also a new heart for investments. Both the great and the very small." ​On the television screen, the news ticker pulsed in garish red, broadcasting multi-billion-dollar outlays and exceptionally favorable loan interest rates for ordinary citizens. ​Adelajda stood motionless before the screen. Held in her grip, the glass creaked under the pressure of her fingers. The massive gold chain resting on her chest heaved violently as the alp drew in a hissing breath scented with fresh coffee. In her sapphire irises danced an icy, azure flame—the harbinger of nightmare and sleep paralysis. ​"Lucjanhir…" she ground out slowly. A note of genuine dread trembled in her velvety voice. "He is in Poland. In Warsaw itself." ​She drew a hand across her neck. Deep furrows appeared on her smooth forehead. ​"Why the hell? Opening a branch, scribbling a signature on a contract, and leaving it to the pawns is one thing, but relocating the main headquarters straight here from Madrid is another entirely. What is he scheming?" ​Cezary Wójcik sat by the kitchen island. Following a recent promotion, he served as a junior police inspector—the equivalent of a lieutenant colonel—in the capital's homicide and organized crime division. He chewed a mouthful of scrambled eggs with bacon, washing it down with strong black tea. Setting his mug on the counter, he wiped his mouth with a napkin and raised his eyes toward the specter. ​"And what are you racking your brain over?" he muttered coldly. "Think logically. Maybe he just wants to keep an eye on Wiktor and the Blood Countess. He pulled them out of the abyss himself and knows perfectly well that Elizabeth is a ticking time bomb that even horse-sized doses of medication might stop keeping in check at any moment. Or maybe he’s keeping an eye on you. You told me about him yourself. Perhaps your old lover simply wants you back." ​Cezary waved his fork toward the living room. ​"Or he’s just expanding his business in that corporate, infernal farce of his. Besides, why jump straight to conspiracy theories? You have that human-skin-bound book of Haber’s right at hand, the one Fugas infused with his power. Check if there’s a fresh entry before you start spreading panic on the carpet. If that fat fiend learned something, he’s bound to expect a handsome payout when you read the new chapter." ​Adelajda flinched. In her eyes, anger gave way to cold calculation. ​"Actually, darling… you're entirely right," she murmured quietly in appreciation. "The devil Fugas always has up-to-date information, despite having been unceremoniously banished from Hell." ​She set down the glass and walked over to the oak dresser. From a drawer, she pulled a heavy volume. Sigmund Haber's book emanated a dull, unpleasant chill. The gold chain around the alp's neck clinked softly as her fingers touched the leather spine. ​She laid the tome on the counter right next to the lieutenant colonel’s plate. Cezary pushed his fork aside. The stench of old parchment, blended with the reek of sulfur, rancid tallow, and burnt bone, killed his appetite in a fraction of a second. ​Adelajda opened the book. The yellowed pages rustled, and the air around them thickened, soaked in an echo of agony. The alp flipped through folios covered in dense Latin until she reached the very end. Fresh phrases indeed appeared on the parchment, dedicated entirely to Lucjanhir. ​The foundations of the deepest dungeons shook when the Morning Star tore the sulfurous mist with his roar. Lucjanhir, a bastard born of a damned human soul, appeared before the face of the Lord of Darkness at a summons of iron and fire. Many fiends waited to see his bones turn to cinder beneath Lucifer’s feet for having willfully torn the rift and dragged Wiktor Adamski—known in Hell as the Blasphemer—along with the Blood Countess, back onto the mortal plane. Yet the bastard did not fall to his knees. The insolent spawn looked into his Father’s blazing eyes as a son, not a slave. ​And a thing occurred that froze the blood in the throats of the tormentors' wardens. Lucifer flicked a clawed hand. He pardoned the bastard. He cared nothing for the two souls plucked from the abyss, and upon that Bavarian bitch Adelajda, who had fled Hell centuries ago, he spat with scorn, deeming their stay upon the earthly plane nothing more than insignificant dust on the winds of ages. ​Yet the grace of the Dark Lord was not free. The bastard received a mission before which demons of higher spheres bent. He was sent to Earth as a guardian and a shadow not for amusement, but to safeguard destiny. When, after a century in hellish fire, the blood of the Blasphemer and the damned serial murderess intertwine, from their abhorrent union may be born the vessel that the chasm has awaited since the dawn of creation. There exists a spark of a chance—faint, slender, yet mightier than the armies of heaven—that from this womb he shall emerge. The Harbinger of the End. The Antichrist in human flesh. ​If Elizabeth conceives by Wiktor, no one—neither mortal, nor angel, nor any of our kind—has the right to touch this seed. Lucjanhir is to be their shield and the eye of the chasm. ​Adelajda froze. Her face turned the color of chalk, and her sapphire eyes widened in disbelief. She drew her hand back from above the faintly steaming page. ​A dead silence fell over the kitchen. ​"Holy fucking shit…" Cezary rasped hoarsely. "Tell me that fat fiend is mocking us again. That this is just the drunken delirium of a devil after way too much moonshine." ​Adelajda did not answer right away. In the air, instead of honey and roses, spread the suffocating reek of swamp rot. ​"Fugas has never lied," she whispered, shedding all aristocratic haughtiness. "Hell doesn't relocate banks for ordinary profit, Cezary. Lucjanhir didn't come here to watch over blood pacts. He came to guard the potential offspring of Elizabeth Báthory and Wiktor." ​The silence was shattered by the shrill ring of a phone. The smartphone lying beside the plate vibrated so violently that it slid across the smooth stone. On the display flashed the name: Emma Jones. ​Adelajda traded a swift glance with Wójcik, then tapped the screen and switched on the speakerphone. ​The ragged breathing of the former agent came through the speaker. In the background, nervous bustling could be heard: the rustle of fabric and a metallic clatter. ​"Adelajda? Are you there?" Emma blurted out nervously. In her usually cool voice resonated profound astonishment. "You won't believe what the fuck just happened here!" ​"Speak, Emma," the alp ground out, gripping the edge of the table so hard that the granite groaned. "Straight to the point." ​"Elizabeth… gained a few pounds, went into a frenzy, and shredded her dresses with her claws. She thought she was swelling up from the lithium and neuroleptics. Burzyński's trusted doctor came over and ran an ultrasound. Adelajda, she's pregnant!" ​The words hung in the kitchen like a lead shroud. The police lieutenant colonel froze, fork in hand. ​"Pregnant…" the alp repeated in a sepulchral whisper. "A body fashioned from the tissues of a dead cow… the damned murderess of Čachtice…" ​"It defies all medicine!" Jones pressed on. "The fetus is growing unnaturally fast, and heat radiates from her lower abdomen like a blast furnace. Wiktor ordered her taken off all pharmaceuticals. Not a single pill, because he fears the drugs will harm the fetus. Which means that for the foreseeable future, we'll be dealing with her homicidal rage and mood swings! Pack your bags, you and Cezary. Wiktor needs all hands on deck!" ​The following weeks in the fortress outside Warsaw turned into a literal purgatory. Wiktor, Emma, Adelajda, and Wójcik walked on eggshells around the countess, while the fetus grew not from week to week, but from day to day. Elizabeth's belly hardened and throbbed with inhuman heat. Her fits of fury were quelled by Wiktor's presence, his power as a blasphemer, and the composure of Emma herself, who managed to appeal to her senses. At last, after five weeks, the hour of delivery arrived. ​A heavy stench of sulfur, blood, and amniotic fluid hung in the air. ​Suddenly, an armored van slammed into the wall enclosing the villa with monstrous force. In that very fraction of a second, the ground-floor windowpanes exploded inward into the living room. ​Through the shattered frames stormed several assault troopers clad in black tactical armor. Silver-embroidered crucifixes and the seals of the Militant Wing of the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith gleamed on their chests. Their armored combat vehicle was already waiting in the driveway with its engine running—they formed the spearhead of the Vatican strike. They had waited for this moment until the very last instant, striking only when everyone's vigilance was lulled by the onset of labor. Fire spat from the muzzles of automatic weapons. They sliced through the air with a hiss, leaving steaming trails: consecrated ammunition of pure silver alloy, ritually quenched in holy water and engraved with verses from the Psalms. ​"Kill the spawn! Slay the vessel!" roared the strike team commander, brandishing a two-handed sword of consecrated steel that glowed with a cold, azure gleam. ​Wiktor threw himself in front of Elizabeth, who lay on the sofa, giving birth in agony. He took a hail of silver rounds to the chest. With inhuman force, the commando leader drove the blade straight into his flank. The steel passed clean through below the ribs, tearing muscle. White smoke erupted from the wound, and dark blood spurted from Wiktor’s mouth. ​The cutthroat was certain he had dispatched the damned soul into oblivion. ​Yet Wiktor did not fall. ​The Blasphemer defied the laws of the sacraments. The consecrated steel hissed, yet it could not break his infernal bond. Adamski roared into his tormentor’s face. His hand flared white-hot. He seized the attacker’s helmet, and the man's skull crunched, melting under the monstrous pressure. ​"Emma, Cezary, shield Elizabeth and our unborn child! Adelajda, help me, please!" Wiktor yelled, spitting blood. She, without waiting for the call, in her ghostly, livid feeding form, was already ripping through the arteries of subsequent riflemen with her purple tongue and talons. ​One of the surviving troopers raised a weapon loaded with consecrated rounds, aiming directly at the bare belly of the laboring countess. ​Cezary Wójcik did not hesitate for a second. On pure instinct, he dove forward, crashed down onto Elizabeth, and shielded her belly with his own back. The Blood Countess looked into his eyes—admiration and gratitude shone in her gaze. ​"Eat this, demon!" the gunman snarled, pulling the trigger. ​Yet no gunshot followed. ​Reality cracked with the dry snap of splintering ice. Between the muzzle and the lieutenant colonel's back materialized a hand of ash-gray skin and black talons. It gripped the barrel opening and effortlessly crushed the hardened steel, tearing the receiver to shreds. ​Lucjanhir appeared unexpectedly in the living room amidst dense plumes of sulfurous smoke. Then, in one fluid motion, he drove his talons into the attacker's solar plexus, ripping out sternum and heart together. The demon turned his burning eyes toward the kneeling Wójcik and bared his fangs in a predatory sneer. ​"Well, well, officer…" he chuckled in a vibrating bass, hauling the cop to his feet by the collar of his suit jacket. "With that single dive, you've most likely earned yourself a permanent stay in my house. But don't you worry: I’ll personally put in a good word with Father for you. Now haul ass! We’re taking their armored rig in the driveway before the rest join the assault! The Vatican has mobilized units from all over Europe!" ​Wiktor, with the hissing blade still lodged deep in his side, scooped the writhing Elizabeth off the sofa. Together with Emma, Adelajda, and Wójcik, they burst through the demolished entrance straight into the black, armored van in which the Vatican spearhead had arrived. Emma leaped behind the wheel and fired up the powerful engine. The armored rig rammed the estate gates, tearing onto the road with a roar… ​Ten minutes later. ​The asphalt of the expressway was torn apart by the roar of engines and the rush of air screaming past at nearly two hundred kilometers per hour. The heavy, factory-armored van of the Vatican spearhead hurtled down the left lane, disregarding all traffic laws. ​Emma Jones gripped the steering wheel so hard that her dark knuckles went white. The vehicle's modified suspension held up, but handling the armored behemoth at that speed demanded absolute precision. ​"Hold this lane, Emma, pedal to the metal, don't slow down!" Lucjanhir roared from the passenger seat. ​The right flank of his earthly vessel was cracking under the onslaught of wounds, vainly trying to seal the gashes left by the consecrated ammunition. Through his shredded shirt poked hard, basalt skin, and embers danced in the corners of his eyes. The right side mirror vanished in a shower of sparks, sheared off by a round of solid silver. The tail was closing in mercilessly—the Vatican executioners paid no heed to collateral damage, raking the fleeing vehicle with full automatic bursts. ​"Fucking Vatican hounds!" the demon spat through clenched fangs. "They're relentless, and they brought backup!" ​From the cargo area came an inhuman howl. Elizabeth Báthory was giving birth in a damned frenzy. ​"Push, damn it, push!" Wójcik hollered. He knelt in a pool of steaming gore, his sleeves smeared with blood. The police lieutenant colonel was delivering the spawn of the Abyss, suppressing the gag reflex brought on by the sickening stench of burning flesh. ​Beside him, Adelajda thrashed. In her ghostly feeding form, she held the countess's hips with her talons, while the heavy gold chain on her chest flared with blinding radiance. ​Strobe lights flickered in Emma's rearview mirror. Three massive, black gunships of the executioners rode their bumper in tight formation. ​Wiktor had no intention of waiting for an execution. One of the rounds would eventually punch through the van's armor and reach his laboring beloved—or worse, one of the mortals: Emma or Cezary. ​He yanked the van's rear latches, shoved the double doors wide open, and leaped into the void behind the speeding vehicle. Twisting midair, he slammed down onto the hood of the left chasing vehicle with tremendous force. ​The laws of physics, bolstered by infernal power, proved ruthless. The mass of nearly a hundred kilograms of pure muscle, reinforced by damned density, crushed the hood, and the rush of wind pinned him against the windshield. Wiktor drove the glowing claws of his left hand into the cowl panel, anchoring himself in the metal. Disregarding the silver blade protruding from his flank, he ripped open his right hand and extended hellish claws, slamming them straight into the composite sheet of armored glass. ​"Get out, you bastards, or I'm coming in!" he bellowed. ​He rammed into the cabin through the shattered glass like a living battering ram. The consecrated steel of the weapons melted in the attackers' hands before they could fire even a single burst. The driver's cervical vertebrae snapped dryly, and the limp vehicle immediately spun around backwards into the crash barrier, throwing off showers of sparks. ​Seeing this, Lucjanhir resolved not to be outdone. He kicked open the armored passenger door and launched himself into the air. ​The demon did not leap blindly. He expertly rode the slipstream trailing the fleeing car and plummeted straight onto the roof of the right vehicle. He absorbed the impact by bending his knees, and the sheet metal beneath his feet caved deep into the cabin. Before the car could lose traction, Lucjanhir sank his claws into the pillar and, with one mighty heave, ripped the entire roof plate away like the lid of a tin can. Inside the exposed cabin, a brief, merciless slaughter erupted. ​The third combat vehicle, seeing the flanks eliminated, downshifted sharply and rammed its bumper into the left side of the car Wiktor was fighting inside. The impact shoved the wreck onto the shoulder. ​Adamski exploited the collision flawlessly. He sprang from the side door of the rammed vehicle straight onto the hood of the center attacker. A second later, Lucjanhir vaulted from the roof of the tumbling right vehicle, landing on the rear section of the armored chassis. ​The two damned entities sank their claws, searing with infernal power, vertically downward, ripping the vehicle's roof in two. ​Wiktor crashed into the front seats. He grabbed the driver by the nape, twisted his vertebrae with a single jerk, and hurled the corpse out through the door he had knocked loose with his shoulder. The cutthroat's body struck the asphalt with horrific force, cartwheeling along the lane and breaking apart. Adamski seized the steering wheel, countered the slide, and stabilized the course of the hijacked machine. ​Lucjanhir slid into the blood-soaked seat beside him, hurling a shattered ballistic helmet out the window. ​"You could have been faster! You let him shoot at me!" the demon snarled, rubbing his shoulder, which was blistered from a consecrated bullet. ​"Quit whining," Adamski muttered coldly. With his left hand, he yanked the hissing silver blade from his side and hurled it onto the road. The tissue inside the wound instantly began to knit together with a faint sizzle. ​He slammed the pedal to the floor, pulling level with the van driven by Emma. ​Through the blown-out windows, Wiktor looked straight at the girl. Relief flashed in her eyes. From inside the cargo area, rising above the engine's roar, suddenly came an entirely new sound. ​The shrill, inhuman, bone-vibrating cry of a newborn. ​The air on the expressway thickened with infernal heat. ​In the mirrors of the captured vehicle, more headlights flared. From behind plumes of smoke emerged three more Vatican vans: massive assault rigs armored in composite and equipped with mechanized turrets. They roared bumper-to-bumper, rapidly closing the gap. ​Heavy barrels extended from the roofs. Bursts of bullets made of pure silver alloy—previously dipped in holy water and ritually quenched—tore through the air. The barrage ripped into the vehicle's sheet metal, and ricochets wreaked havoc inside the cabin. Every hit seared black, smoking furrows into Lucjanhir's flesh. ​The bastard leaned out through the shattered window, sank his claws into the chassis, and roared directly into the leaden clouds: ​"Father! Do you see this?!" His voice unleashed a shockwave. "They have consecrated weapons! I know I am only your bastard! But haul your ass over here, because without your help, we all die right here!" ​The silence that struck his consciousness a fraction of a second later was denser than a vacuum. The roar of the engines died away. ​In the depths of his mind reverberated the bass rumble of crushing planets: ​"Within your veins flows my blood. Within your fist rests my power. Rise and slaughter them, my son. I pour into you the black wings of the Abyss—not as a mercy, but as a weapon. The time of the bastard is ended. From this moment forth, you are a true-blooded heir of the Chasm. Dare not know mercy. Turn them to ashes in my name." ​Lucjanhir's body erupted in black flame. ​The bones on his forehead cracked with a dry snap, stretching into massive, curved horns of black obsidian. His skin hardened, taking on the texture of basalt through which boiling sulfur gleamed. From his shoulder blades, tearing through muscle and the remnants of his suit, erupted massive, leathery wings tipped with keratinized talons. Their wingspan unleashed a gust that swept the hail of lead aside in mid-flight. ​Wiktor glanced at his passenger with a predatory grin. ​"Well…" he drawled. "Now you can really take flight. Wouldn't mind a pair of those myself." ​Lucjanhir launched himself from the window frame. The stroke of his wings bent the roof pillars and hurled the demon vertically into the air with the speed of thunder. ​Subterranean chambers of the Apostolic Palace, Vatican City. Command Center of the Militant Wing of the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith. ​An icy chill gripped the windowless bunker. The space was filled with the steady hum of servers cooled by liquid nitrogen. On the stark walls, crucifixes bearing relics hung alongside panoramic monitors displaying telemetry and etheric resonance readings. ​The main wall display broadcast a feed from a spy satellite positioned over the highway outside Warsaw. ​The three second-wave assault vans ceased to exist in the blink of an eye. The display showed only mangled wreckage: two had been crushed by a vertical strike with the force of a meteorite, the third cleaved lengthwise down its chassis. Above the burning convoy hovered a winged signature, swallowing all light. ​In the corner of the screen, a red alert flashed, signaling a violent spike in etheric radiation emanating from inside the retreating black van. ​"Dominus Iesus…" whispered a young prelate, dropping his rosary onto the console. ​The cardinal commanding the operation stepped up to the console. He rested his hands on the edge of the operations table, fixing his gaze on the extinguishing telemetry blips of his men. ​"Report," he said flatly. ​"Sections Alpha, Bravo, and Charlie of the second wave… destroyed, Your Eminence," the officer reported in a breaking voice. "No survivors. Telemetry indicates a full demonic emanation of princely rank. Some entity has obtained the direct support of Lucifer. We do not know whether it is Wiktor or someone else." ​The cardinal did not bat an eye. His gaze settled on the violet-black blot pulsing inside the fleeing van. The pulse was twofold: one fading, damned, belonging to the resurrected murderess… and the second. Fresh, glowing with inhuman density. ​"The veil has torn," the prelate added in a whisper. "The Blood Countess has given birth." ​The cardinal straightened slowly. He looked at the crucifix hanging above the consoles, its gold darkening in a strange manner, then reached for the red, encrypted phone resting in an armored alcove. ​"Connect me to the Holy Father's apartments," he commanded in an icy tone. "Wake His Holiness. The militant wing has suffered defeat, and the blood of the damned has borne fruit. Alert the basilicas and nunciatures across Europe. The wolf cub of the Chasm has arrived in this world." ​They reached the safe haven of an abandoned, derelict building tucked out of the way. The van rolled into a cold, musty garage with its wheels locked, marking the concrete floor with a thick streak of burnt rubber and steaming fluids from the punctured radiator. ​As soon as the choked engine died, Adelajda's hysterical, gut-wrenching shriek tore through the cargo hold. ​"Cezary! Cezary, don't close your eyes, I'm begging you, look at me, don't close your eyes! Don't you dare die on me now!" screamed the alp, and in her trembling voice not a trace remained of the former, haughty aristocrat from the Bavarian realm. There was only the pure, animal panic of an entity that had just realized her mortal chosen one was slipping into oblivion. ​Only now, once the adrenaline of the frantic pursuit had ebbed and Elizabeth had brought the spawn into the world, did Lieutenant Colonel Wójcik's fragile body unconditionally succumb to the laws of biology. ​One of the stray, consecrated silver-alloy bullets fired by the Vatican rig's mechanized turret had punched through the rear panel of the van and driven itself violently under the officer's right ribs. The round had massacred his liver, shredding the tissue into a bloody pulp. The cop had stayed upright on sheer willpower alone, shielding the newborn with his own body to the very end. The internal hemorrhage, however, proved merciless. The abdominal cavity flooded with dark blood within dozens of seconds. Wójcik collapsed limply onto the corrugated sheet metal of the truck bed with a dull thud, and from his cyanotic lips escaped a final, frothing breath. ​The gold chain around Adelajda's neck went dark in a fraction of a second, shrinking and dulling like a scrap of rusted lead. She sobbed, forcing her own icy breath into his mouth, attempting to infuse his body with vital energy. She yanked at his cooling hands, yet the mortal's soul slipped from the dead flesh like a wisp of smoke in the wind. It was too late. ​Absolute, bottomless blackness swallowed Cezary. ​Everything drew to a close in a single heartbeat. A moment later, he plummeted into the abyss at crushing speed. Heaven had shut its gates before him, delivering a damned verdict. And yet it had been nothing more than a human instinct—he had tried to shield the Blood Countess and her newborn infant with his own body. The deed was noble, and the punishment dictated by the unyielding ruthlessness of Heaven. In human terms, no one in his shoes would have deserved such damnation. ​Crashing onto hard ground robbed him of his remaining senses. Beneath his bare palms, he felt black basalt, scalding and slick with damned tallow. The air was unfit for breathing—a dense suspension of boiling sulfur, charred meat, and rancid fat. Beneath monumental vaults arched from bone drifted the deafening wail of millions of souls, woven into the rhythmic thud of infernal bellows. Before he could grasp his own nakedness, thick, glowing chains wrapped around his arms, biting with a hiss into the tissue of his newly formed, infernal vessel. ​In the Chasm, time lost all meaning. Every earthly minute could stretch into the agony of entire centuries or shrink into a painful blink of an eye. Wójcik trudged forward, shoved along in an endless column of the damned, wading ankle-deep in lakes of steaming bile, until at last he stood before a monumental black block. ​Above the stone dais towered an executioner demon—an eyeless, hulking mass with arms of ash and flesh dripping with boiling tar. The beast wasted no time; the queue was waiting. In its massive paw was clenched a scourge woven of red-hot wires and rusted hooks. ​The whistle of sliced air rang out. ​The first strike. ​The incandescent metal bit into Wójcik's shoulder blades with an inhuman crack, tearing a strip of skin and muscle down to the white bone of his spine. The pain was absolute, metaphysical—it seared the soul to its very core. ​The second strike. ​The scourge lashed across, wrapping around his torso and ripping smoking furrows along his right side—in the exact spot where the silver lead had torn through him on Earth. ​Cezary bit his teeth until blood came, refusing to utter a whimper. He braced himself for an eternity of slaughter. For assisting monsters, for falsifying records of Báthory’s crimes, for opening his heart to an Alp, and for aiding in the birth of an infernal bastard—he knew that Up Above, nobody indulged in mitigating circumstances. The gates of Heaven had slammed shut before him irrevocably. ​The demon raised its arm a third time, tensing swollen sinews to rip the condemned man in two. ​Yet in a split second, the blow froze in mid-air. ​From the dense, sulfurous vapors resounded a deep, vibrating resonance. The executioner slowly lowered the blood-drenched whip. Instead of continuing the torment, it bowed its hideous face over the kneeling mortal. In its jaw, split to the bone, fury was no more. Across exposed fangs dripping with blackness bloomed a slow, ghastly smile of boundless satisfaction and respect. ​From the demon's maw came a raspy rumble: ​"The order of the Supreme, damned one. Merely twice with the lash for your two merits. That will suffice." ​The executioner's talons opened, and the red-hot chains snapped with a dry clatter, crumbling to ash. Before Wójcik could raise his head, the rift of reality beneath his feet collapsed, and a tremendous pull sucked him back into the scarlet vortex. ​Cezary choked on the air with a hoarse, agonal gasp, like a drowned man washed ashore. ​He lay on the blood-spattered concrete of the abandoned derelict. Beside him, Adelajda remained on her knees, petrified. Her lips trembled with terror. Above them both stood Lucjanhir. From the bastard's back—now a mighty prince of the Abyss—rose proud, black, leathery wings, casting off the suffocating reek of burning from the highway massacre. The demon's hand, still smoking from tearing the fabric of dimensions, pressed down on the policeman's chest. ​On Earth, mere minutes had passed since his death. In the Abyss—for his soul—an entire hour could have gone by… ​Lucjanhir bared his cracked fangs in a wide, predatory grin, wiping the cuff of his suit clean of remaining gore. ​"I told you, officer, I’d put in a good word with Father for you," the demon chortled in a deep, tectonic bass that rattled the windowpanes of the derelict. "The executioner struck you with the whip only twice. Two blows for merits, Cezary. The first time, back at the villa, you threw yourself like a rabid hound upon the countess to shield her belly from bullets with your own body. The second… well, fine, you just happened to be standing in the line of fire when the turret opened up, which doesn't change the fact that you took consecrated silver right to the guts. Down there, they made an express exception for you. Few mortals can boast that Lucifer himself signed their return ticket and ordered the whip lowered." ​With a trembling hand slick with sweat, Wójcik clutched his right side beneath his torn shirt. The skin was cool, firm, and completely intact. Of the fatal gunshot and the infernal lashes, nothing remained but a pale, fading scar. ​A few meters away, leaning against a dusty pallet of old cement bags, rested Elizabeth Báthory. Her pitch-black eyes glowed with the half-deranged, former triumph of Čachtice. Reconstructed from bovine tissue, the countess's body steamed with inhuman heat, and upon her bloodstained forearm lay the newborn child. A boy. He was pale, tiny, and beneath his skin pulsed threads of living fire. The infant greedily drank milk from her breast, letting out not a single human whimper—only a deep, guttural purr. ​Beside them, with a smoldering cigarette between his teeth, stood Wiktor. In the former cop's narrowed eyes gleamed the ruthless pride of a father. ​The countess raised her eyes to Cezary as he rose from his knees. On her full, blood-smeared lips blossomed a languid smile dripping with sensuality. ​"I am glad you returned, Cezary…" she purred in a velvety, hypnotic voice, cradling the little damned creature in her arms. "Would you like to hold him? Come closer, do not be afraid, he does not bite anymore. After all, you are his godfather now. Thank you for everything. Know that I am grateful to you. As is Wiktor." ​Lucjanhir smiled crookedly, as though listening to something extraordinarily intriguing. ​"Your torments, even when you eventually meet your end and return to Hell, have been definitively concluded," the demon tossed out casually, looking down at Wójcik and flicking dust from his shoulder. "Twice. No further roasting, no torments. Who knows, perhaps with a bit of luck, they’ll even carve out some modest chamber for you in my father's basalt palace, in the wing for honored guests. Besides… the same goes for you, Jones." ​The demon shifted his gaze to the hitherto silent Emma, who was still leaning against the hood of the van, methodically loading a spare magazine for her pistol. ​"You handled that vehicle quite exemplarily," he chuckled softly. "I mentioned you to Father as well. Besides, he saw and felt everything himself from the very bottom of the Abyss. With your latest record and that stunt on the highway, your place in Hell is guaranteed. But no worries, you’ll get a couple of lashes upon arrival to welcome you, purely for the sake of formality." He snorted with guttural laughter. ​He turned his head toward Adelajda. The Germanic alp had already risen from her knees, though her sapphire eyes still glistened with tears, and the necklace extinguished a moment ago was slowly regaining a faint, golden luster, drinking in Lucjanhir's dark energy. ​"And you, my dear Adelajda?" he drawled with a predatory, familiar note of sensual insolence. "Perhaps it would be fitting to finally thank me for this little miracle? I know full well what our turbulent past looked like and under what circumstances you fled my dungeons, but in the end, I dragged your current favorite out of the chasm itself. I did it for him, as well as for you… though you know full well I still have an unquenchable appetite for you." ​Adelajda let out a long, heavy sigh from her lungs. Swallowing the pride of a former Bavarian duchess, she stepped a pace closer and gave a slight nod with cold, impeccable grace: ​"I must give you credit and offer my sincere thanks, Lucjanhir. You kept your word." ​"Splendid, then!" the demon clapped his hands, and with a soft rustle, his great black wings folded along his back and melted beneath his skin, vanishing without a trace. "Fine work, my dears. Now we await transport with my people. I've arranged for site security and evacuation through Prosperity Bank's private security firm. They are ordinary mortals, so be kind enough to put on your human masks. Adelajda, reel that tongue back in. And you, Wiktor… quench those veins of yours, tuck away that hellfire, and try to resemble a human rather than a freshly unleashed demon." ​At that moment, the floorboards and cement pallets creaked. Elizabeth Báthory rose slowly from her makeshift bed. The newborn creature, sated on her milk, was already sleeping quietly, wrapped in Wójcik's bloodstained jacket, while a thin wisp of gray steam drifted from its tiny nose. ​The countess straightened the shredded silk of her gown, and upon her pale, aristocratic face—twisted over the past five weeks in animal madness—appeared an expression of human exhaustion and a strange, unsettling embarrassment. ​"Do… do you have my medical kit anywhere?" she asked quietly, her velvety voice raspy and trembling slightly. She looked first at Wiktor, then shifted her gaze to Emma and Cezary. "May I take my medication now? And… forgive me. For these past weeks, for that frenzy. I know how unbearable I can be when my senses refuse to obey me." ​Lucjanhir froze mid-step. He stared at her, then ostentatiously slapped his forehead with an open palm. ​"I don't believe it… I just fucking don't believe it!" he burst out laughing, shaking his head in disbelief. "The Blood Countess, the butcher of Čachtice, apologizing to mortals for bad manners?! Oh boy, Hell has officially frozen solid, that's for damn sure! I wonder what my old man will say when he feels that sudden Arctic breeze down at the bottom of the Abyss!" title: Die Mythen. Chapter 33: Merits
summary: ​Chapter 33: Merits ​"A warm welcome to our capital. We are immensely honored that Prosperity Bank chose Warsaw of all places as the site of its headquarters in this part of Europe," the city mayor solemnly proclaimed, turning toward the lenses of over a dozen cameras with a practiced smile. ​The flash of cameras reflected in the polished granite lobby of the skyscraper at Rondo Daszyńskiego. With a quiet, dry snap, the scissors sliced through the thick ribbon, clearing the path to the elevators leading to the top floors, where the management of the new financial powerhouse was housed. ​The man standing beside the city's leader looked impeccable. A suit of Italian wool fit him like a second skin, and an understated signet ring set with a black stone drew the eyes of female journalists. An unnatural, predatory elegance radiated from him. ​"Thank you, Mr. Mayor," he replied in a deep, velvety timbre. He accepted the microphone with cosmopolitan grace. "The Polish market is pivotal to our institution. I personally took the trouble to master your language. Please forgive my harsh, foreign accent; it is an exceedingly difficult tongue. I hope, however, that Prosperity Bank will become for Warsaw and its residents not only a symbol of stability, but also a new heart for investments. Both the great and the very small." ​On the television screen, the news ticker pulsed in garish red, broadcasting multi-billion-dollar outlays and exceptionally favorable loan interest rates for ordinary citizens. ​Adelajda stood motionless before the screen. Held in her grip, the glass creaked under the pressure of her fingers. The massive gold chain resting on her chest heaved violently as the alp drew in a hissing breath scented with fresh coffee. The newborn creature, sated on her milk, was already sleeping quietly, wrapped in Wójcik's bloodstained jacket, while a thin wisp of gray steam drifted from its tiny nose. ​The countess straightened the shredded silk of her gown, and upon her pale, aristocratic face—twisted over the past five weeks in animal madness—appeared an expression of human exhaustion and a strange, unsettling embarrassment. ​"Do… do you have my medical kit anywhere?" she asked quietly, her velvety voice raspy and trembling slightly. She looked first at Wiktor, then shifted her gaze to Emma and Cezary. "May I take my medication now? And… forgive me. For these past weeks, for that frenzy. I know how unbearable I can be when my senses refuse to obey me." ​Lucjanhir froze mid-step. He stared at her, then ostentatiously slapped his forehead with an open palm. ​"I don't believe it… I just fucking don't believe it!" he burst out laughing, shaking his head in disbelief. "The Blood Countess, the butcher of Čachtice, apologizing to mortals for bad manners?! Oh boy, Hell has officially frozen solid, that's for damn sure! I wonder what my old man will say when he feels that sudden Arctic breeze down at the bottom of the Abyss!" title: Ağıralioğlu: Okul öncesinden başlayarak çocuklara her okul günü en az bir öğün yemek vereceğiz
summary: Anahtar Parti Genel Başkanı Yavuz Ağıralioğlu, yeni eğitim öğretim yılının başlamasıyla birlikte öğrencilerin beslenmesine ilişkin açıklamalarda bulundu. Ağıralioğlu, partisinin iktidarında okul öncesinden başlayarak öğrencilere her okul günü en az bir öğün sağlıklı yemek verileceğini söyledi. Ağıralioğlu, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamada bazı çocukların okula beslenme çantasıyla, bazılarının ise boş çantayla gittiğini belirterek, bu durumun eğitimde fırsat eşitliği açısından sorun oluşturduğunu ifade etti. “Çocuklarımızın bir kısmı okula beslenme çantasıyla, bir kısmı boş çantayla gidiyor. Birinin önünde sütü, yumurtası, meyvesi var; ötekinin karnı aç” diyen Ağıralioğlu, öğrencilerin aynı sınıfta okuyup aynı sınava girdiğini belirtti. “Aç çocukla tok çocuğu aynı sıraya oturtup fırsat eşitliği diyemezsiniz” Çocukların yeterince beslenememesinin zihinsel ve bedensel gelişimlerini etkilediğini savunan Ağıralioğlu, “Aç çocukla tok çocuğu aynı sıraya oturtup buna eğitimde fırsat eşitliği diyemezsiniz” ifadelerini kullandı. Ağıralioğlu, partisinin iktidarında uygulanacağını belirttiği program kapsamında öğrencilere protein, sebze ve meyve içeren en az bir öğün yemek verileceğini söyledi. “Bu memleketin evladı okulda aç oturmayacak” diyen Ağıralioğlu, uygulamanın 17 milyon çocuk için yaklaşık 150 milyar liralık kaynak gerektireceğini ifade etti. “Bütçenin yüzde birinden azı” Ağıralioğlu, söz konusu kaynağın Türkiye’nin bir yıllık milli gelirinin yaklaşık binde ikisine, merkezi yönetim bütçesinin ise yüzde birinden daha azına karşılık geldiğini belirtti. “Bir devlet, bütçesinin yüzde birinden azını 17 milyon evladının sağlıklı beslenmesine ayıramıyorsa neye ayıracak?” diye soran Ağıralioğlu, programın yalnızca öğrencilere yemek sağlanmasıyla sınırlı olmayacağını söyledi. Çiftçi ve kooperatifler de programa dahil edilecek Ağıralioğlu, planlanan sistemde Anadolu’daki çiftçiler ve kooperatiflerin de yer alacağını belirterek, yerel üretim, süt, yumurta, meyve ve coğrafi işaretli ürünlerin çocukların beslenmesinde kullanılacağını ifade etti. Programla hem çiftçilerin ürünlerine pazar oluşturulmasının hem de kooperatiflerin desteklenmesinin hedeflendiğini belirten Ağıralioğlu, “Çiftçinin ürettiğini, milletin evladının sofrasıyla buluşturmaktır” dedi. title: İçişleri Bakanlığı duyurdu: 6 bin 134 kişinin vatandaşlığı iptal edildi
summary: Bakanlık, İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığının yürüttüğü son soruşturmada ise 1.070 kişinin usulsüz şekilde vatandaşlık kazandığının belirlendiğini duyurdu. İçişleri Bakanlığı, yatırım yoluyla Türk vatandaşlığı edinme süreçlerine ilişkin açıklama yaptı. Bakanlık, başvuruların 5901 sayılı Türk Vatandaşlığı Kanunu ve ilgili mevzuat kapsamında yürütüldüğünü belirtti. Açıklamaya göre, yatırım uygunluk belgesinin alınmasının ardından başvuru sahipleri hakkında Emniyet Genel Müdürlüğü ve Milli İstihbarat Teşkilatı Başkanlığı tarafından güvenlik soruşturması ve arşiv araştırması yapılıyor. Olumlu sonuçlanan başvurular ise Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü tarafından sonuçlandırılıyor. Bakanlık, sahte ve usulsüz ekspertiz raporlarıyla vatandaşlık sürecini suistimal etmeye çalışanlara yönelik Tapu ve Kadastro Genel Müdürlüğü, Vergi Denetim Kurulu Başkanlığı ve Emniyet Genel Müdürlüğü tarafından yürütülen incelemelerin sonuçlarını açıkladı. Buna göre 1.150 yatırımcının yatırım uygunluk belgesi iptal edildi. Bu yatırımcıların aile fertleriyle birlikte toplam 5 bin 391 kişinin vatandaşlık kararı iptal edildi. Vatandaşlık aldıktan sonra kamu düzeni ve milli güvenlik bakımından sakıncalı olduğu tespit edilen 263 yatırımcı ile aile fertlerinden oluşan toplam 743 kişinin de vatandaşlık kararı geri alındı. Böylece toplam 1.413 yatırımcı ile aile fertleri dahil 6 bin 134 kişinin vatandaşlık kazanma kararı iptal edildi veya geri alındı. 11 Şubat’tan bu yana 1.400 kişi hakkında işlem Bakanlık, 11 Şubat 2026'dan itibaren yapılan işlemlere ilişkin de bilgi verdi. Bu tarihten itibaren yatırım uygunluk belgesi iptal edilen 458 yatırımcı ve aile fertleri olmak üzere toplam 1.393 kişinin vatandaşlığının iptal edildiği belirtildi. Ayrıca 7 kişinin vatandaşlığının, milli güvenlik ve kamu düzeni bakımından sakınca bulunması nedeniyle geri alındığı kaydedildi. İstanbul soruşturmasında 1.070 kişi tespit edildi İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığınca 21 Eylül 2026'da yürütülen soruşturma kapsamında ise muvazaalı gayrimenkul satışları üzerinden usulsüz şekilde Türk vatandaşlığı kazandırıldığı belirlenen aile bireyleriyle birlikte 1.070 kişi tespit edildi. Bakanlık, vatandaşlık edinme süreci devam eden 11 kişinin de belirlendiğini açıkladı. Yapılan incelemede 1.070 kişinin 263'ünün yatırımcı, 807'sinin ise aile ferdi olduğu tespit edildi. Bu kişilerden 1.015'inin karar tarihinde, 55 çocuğun ise karar tarihinden sonra Türk vatandaşlığını kazandığı belirlendi. Vatandaşlık süreci devam eden 11 kişiden biri hakkında geri alma, üçü hakkında ret işlemi yapıldı. Yedi kişinin ise vatandaşlık başvurusunda bulunmadığı tespit edildi. Bakanlık: Personel kaynaklı zafiyet veya ihmal yok İçişleri Bakanlığı, soruşturmaya konu işlemlerin başvuru öncesi belgelere ilişkin sahtecilik girişimleri olduğunu belirterek, Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü personelinin görev ve yetkileri kapsamında herhangi bir zafiyet veya ihmal bulunmadığını savundu. Açıklamada, “Suç teşkil eden tüm usulsüzlükler adli makamlara intikal ettirilmektedir” denildi.
